q: What is the maximum number of IAM users you can create in a single AWS account?

exp.b: Correct. You can create a maximum of 5,000 IAM users per AWS account. For more users, use temporary credentials or IAM Identity Center.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a fixed limit of 5,000.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM groups per AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Correct. You can create a maximum of 300 IAM groups per AWS account.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM groups a single IAM user can belong to?

exp.a: Incorrect. A user can belong to more than 5 groups.
exp.b: Correct. A single IAM user can be a member of up to 10 IAM groups.
exp.c: Incorrect. 15 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of managed policies that can be attached to an IAM user, group, or role?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 5.
exp.b: Correct. Up to 10 managed policies can be attached to a single IAM user, group, or role.
exp.c: Incorrect. 15 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of access keys per IAM user?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 access key is allowed.
exp.b: Correct. Each IAM user can have a maximum of 2 access keys, which facilitates key rotation without downtime.
exp.c: Incorrect. 3 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM roles per AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. 500 is below the default limit.
exp.b: Correct. The default maximum number of IAM roles per AWS account is 1,000 (this is a soft limit that can be increased).
exp.c: Incorrect. 5,000 is the user limit, not roles.

q: How many MFA devices can be assigned to a single IAM user?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 MFA device can be assigned.
exp.b: Incorrect. More than 2 can be assigned.
exp.c: Incorrect. More than 5 can be assigned.

q: What is the maximum size of an IAM managed policy?

exp.a: Incorrect. 2,048 characters is the limit for inline policies on users and role trust policies.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum size of a managed policy is 6,144 characters (not including whitespace).
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,240 characters exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum size of an IAM role trust policy?

exp.a: Correct. The maximum size of a role trust policy is 2,048 characters.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4,096 characters exceeds the trust policy limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. 6,144 characters is the managed policy limit.

q: What is the maximum session duration for an IAM role when assumed?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is the default but not the maximum.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 hours is below the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. IAM roles can have a maximum session duration of 12 hours (configurable from 1 hour to 12 hours).

q: What is the default duration of temporary credentials issued by AWS STS (AssumeRole)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 15 minutes is the minimum, not the default.
exp.b: Correct. The default duration for STS temporary credentials via AssumeRole is 1 hour (3,600 seconds).

q: What is the minimum and maximum duration range for STS temporary credentials (AssumeRole)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 minutes is below the minimum.
exp.b: Correct. STS credentials can be configured from 15 minutes (900 seconds) minimum to 12 hours (43,200 seconds) maximum.

q: What is the maximum session duration for IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO)?

exp.a: Incorrect. Sessions can last longer.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 hours is not the maximum.

q: What is the automatic rotation period for AWS KMS customer managed keys (default when enabled)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days is not the default rotation period.
exp.b: Incorrect. 90 days is the minimum configurable, not the default.
exp.c: Correct. When enabled, AWS KMS automatically rotates KMS keys every 365 days (1 year) by default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 730 days is not the default.

q: What is the configurable range for KMS automatic key rotation?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days is below the minimum.
exp.b: Correct. KMS allows configuring automatic key rotation between 90 and 2,560 days (approximately 7 years).
exp.c: Incorrect. This is not the correct range.
exp.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct range.

q: What is the waiting period for KMS key deletion?

exp.a: Incorrect. KMS keys cannot be immediately deleted.
exp.b: Correct. When you schedule a KMS key for deletion, there is a mandatory waiting period of 7 to 30 days (default 30 days) during which the key can be recovered.
exp.c: Incorrect. The maximum waiting period is 30 days.

q: What is the monthly cost of a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in AWS KMS?

exp.a: Incorrect. Customer managed keys are not free (AWS managed keys are free).
exp.b: Correct. Customer managed KMS keys cost $1 per month per key, plus $0.03 per 10,000 API requests.
exp.c: Incorrect. $5 exceeds the cost.

q: What is the KMS API request cost?

exp.a: Incorrect. $0.01 is below the cost.
exp.b: Correct. KMS charges $0.03 per 10,000 API requests for cryptographic operations.
exp.c: Incorrect. $0.10 exceeds the cost.

q: What is the KMS API request limit (symmetric encrypt/decrypt) per second per Region?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is higher.
exp.b: Correct. The shared KMS request quota for cryptographic operations is approximately 5,500 requests per second per Region (varies by Region, can be increased).
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the default shared quota.

q: What is the maximum data size that can be directly encrypted by a single KMS API call?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 KB is below the limit.
exp.b: Correct. KMS can directly encrypt up to 4 KB (4,096 bytes) of data per API call. For larger data, use envelope encryption.
exp.c: Incorrect. 16 KB exceeds the limit.

q: What FIPS validation level does AWS CloudHSM meet?

exp.a: Incorrect. Level 1 is the lowest validation.
exp.b: Incorrect. Level 2 is not the CloudHSM level.
exp.c: Correct. AWS CloudHSM uses FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules.
exp.d: Incorrect. Level 4 is the highest and not applicable to CloudHSM.

q: What is the cost per month for a general-purpose AWS Private CA?

exp.b: Correct. The default WCU limit is 1,500 per Web ACL, which can be increased to 5,000 maximum.

q: A high-traffic application using S3 with SSE-KMS is getting ThrottlingException errors at 6,000 requests/second. What is the cause and solution?

opts.a: S3 rate limits; use multipart upload
opts.b: KMS API rate limit (~5,500/sec) exceeded; use S3 Bucket Keys to reduce KMS calls by 99%

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 doesn't typically cause ThrottlingException for KMS.
exp.b: Correct. Each S3 GET/PUT with SSE-KMS calls KMS, hitting the ~5,500 req/sec quota. S3 Bucket Keys generate a bucket-level key that creates data keys within S3, reducing KMS calls by up to 99%.
exp.c: Incorrect. IAM restrictions cause AccessDenied, not Throttling.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda is not involved in S3 encryption.

q: A company needs to encrypt 10 GB of data using KMS. The KMS Encrypt API only handles 4 KB. What approach should they use?

opts.a: Split data into 4 KB chunks and call KMS for each
opts.b: Use envelope encryption: generate a data key from KMS, encrypt data locally with the data key, store encrypted data key alongside ciphertext
opts.d: Upload to S3 and let KMS handle it

exp.a: Incorrect. This would generate millions of KMS API calls and be extremely slow.
exp.b: Correct. Envelope encryption uses KMS to generate/encrypt a data key, then uses that data key locally to encrypt the large data. Only the 4 KB data key goes through KMS.
exp.c: Incorrect. SSE-S3 is only for S3 storage.
exp.d: Incorrect. This only works for S3 and doesn't address the 4 KB limit.

q: A developer configures a Lambda function with an IAM role that has 12 managed policies attached. What happens?

opts.a: It works fine; there's no limit
opts.b: The attachment fails because the maximum is 10 managed policies per role
opts.c: Only the first 10 policies are applied
opts.d: The role is automatically converted to an admin role

exp.a: Incorrect. There is a limit.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum is 10 managed policies per IAM entity (user, group, or role). Attaching the 11th policy will fail. Use inline policies or consolidate policies to stay within limits.
exp.c: Incorrect. AWS doesn't partially apply policies.

q: An organization has 5,000 IAM users and needs to onboard 1,000 more employees. What should they do?

opts.b: Use IAM Identity Center or federation with an external IdP since the 5,000 IAM user limit has been reached
opts.d: Request a quota increase for IAM users

exp.a: Incorrect. The 5,000 user limit has been reached.
exp.b: Correct. The 5,000 IAM user limit is a hard limit. For additional users, use IAM Identity Center (SSO) or federate with an external identity provider (SAML/OIDC) which provides temporary credentials without creating IAM users.
exp.c: Incorrect. While possible, federation is the proper solution.
exp.d: Incorrect. The 5,000 IAM user limit cannot be increased.

q: A security team needs to ensure KMS key deletion doesn't cause data loss. They want the maximum time to recover a key before permanent deletion. What should they set?

exp.a: Incorrect. 7 days is the minimum and provides the least recovery time.
exp.b: Correct. Setting the maximum 30-day waiting period provides the most time to discover and cancel the deletion if needed. During this period, the key can be recovered.
exp.c: Incorrect. 90 days exceeds the maximum configurable period.
exp.d: Incorrect. While valid, the question asks about the waiting period.

q: An application processes 2 million KMS encryption requests per second during peak hours. The Region's KMS quota is 5,500 requests/sec. What solutions reduce KMS API calls?

opts.b: Implement data key caching (AWS Encryption SDK), use S3 Bucket Keys, and request quota increase
opts.c: Switch to client-side encryption without KMS

exp.a: Incorrect. Quota increases alone may not be sufficient for 2M req/sec.
exp.b: Correct. Combining data key caching (reuses keys for multiple operations), S3 Bucket Keys (for S3 workloads), and quota increases provides a comprehensive solution to handle 2M req/sec.
exp.c: Incorrect. Losing KMS management is a security tradeoff.
exp.d: Incorrect. Multiple accounts add complexity without solving the core issue.

q: A company has Security Group rules allowing SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0. They have 60 inbound rules already. They want to add more specific IP ranges but can't. What's the issue?

opts.b: The Security Group has reached its default maximum of 60 inbound rules
opts.c: The VPC doesn't support more rules

exp.a: Incorrect. NACLs are separate from SG rules limits.
exp.b: Correct. The default limit is 60 inbound rules per Security Group. To add more, either request a quota increase, consolidate rules using CIDR ranges, or use prefix lists.
exp.c: Incorrect. VPCs don't limit SG rules.
exp.d: Incorrect. AWS doesn't globally block SSH.

q: A network admin is troubleshooting connectivity. Traffic is allowed by the Security Group (stateful) but blocked. They check NACLs and find the outbound rule allows traffic but there's no matching inbound return rule. What's the problem?

opts.b: NACLs are stateless — return traffic must be explicitly allowed in both directions

exp.a: Incorrect. Security Groups are stateful (return traffic is automatic).
exp.b: Correct. Unlike Security Groups, NACLs are stateless. Both inbound AND outbound rules must explicitly allow traffic (including ephemeral port ranges for return traffic).
exp.c: Incorrect. VPC peering is not indicated.
exp.d: Incorrect. Route tables are separate from NACLs.

q: A WAF Web ACL has reached 1,500 WCU and the team needs to add more rules. What should they do?

opts.b: Request a WCU quota increase (up to 5,000 maximum) through AWS Support

exp.a: Incorrect. A new Web ACL would have the same default limit.
exp.b: Correct. The default 1,500 WCU can be increased up to 5,000 WCU maximum by requesting a quota increase through AWS Support.
exp.c: Incorrect. Removing rules reduces protection.
exp.d: Incorrect. Network Firewall serves a different purpose.

q: A company wants to block login attempts exceeding 100 per 5 minutes from a single IP. Which WAF feature and configuration do they need?

opts.b: Rate-based rule with threshold of 100 requests per 5-minute window scoped to the login URI

exp.a: Incorrect. Geo-match blocks by country, not request rate.
exp.b: Correct. A rate-based rule with 100 as the rate limit (minimum allowed), scoped to the login URI path, will automatically block IPs exceeding 100 requests per 5 minutes.
exp.c: Incorrect. Bot Control categorizes bots but doesn't set custom rate limits.
exp.d: Incorrect. String-match rules don't track request rates.

q: A company using Shield Advanced experiences a DDoS attack causing $50,000 in CloudFront data transfer costs. How can they recover?

opts.b: Request DDoS cost protection credits from Shield Advanced for the verified attack
opts.d: Get a free month of Shield Advanced

exp.a: Incorrect. Shield Advanced includes cost protection.
exp.b: Correct. Shield Advanced provides cost protection credits for scaling charges (CloudFront, ALB, Route 53, etc.) incurred during verified DDoS attacks. Contact the DDoS Response Team (DRT) to initiate.
exp.c: Incorrect. AWS provides credits directly.
exp.d: Incorrect. A free month is not the mechanism.

q: An organization needs their CloudTrail data retained for 7 years for compliance. They want SQL-query capability. Which option is most cost-effective?

exp.a: Incorrect. At $2.50/GB this is 10x more expensive than 7-year retention.
exp.b: Correct. The 7-year retention tier at $0.25/GB ingested is specifically designed for long-term compliance storage with pay-per-scan query pricing.
exp.c: Incorrect. While viable, it requires managing partitioning and storage; Lake is simpler.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs for 7 years would be very expensive.

q: A Cognito User Pool has 50 custom attributes already configured. The team needs to add one more. What happens?

opts.b: The addition fails because the maximum of 50 custom attributes has been reached
opts.c: An older attribute is automatically deleted

exp.a: Incorrect. The 50-attribute limit has been reached.
exp.b: Correct. Cognito User Pools have a hard limit of 50 custom attributes. The team would need to consolidate existing attributes or store additional data elsewhere.
exp.c: Incorrect. Attributes are not automatically deleted.
exp.d: Incorrect. This is a hard limit that cannot be increased.

q: A user has 2 active access keys and needs a new one for a new application. What must they do first?

opts.b: Delete or deactivate one of the existing 2 access keys before creating a new one
opts.c: Contact AWS Support to increase the limit
opts.d: Use the root account key instead

exp.a: Incorrect. The maximum is 2 access keys per user.
exp.b: Correct. Since the hard limit is 2 access keys per IAM user, one must be deleted or deactivated before creating a new one. This limit facilitates key rotation (old key + new key during transition).
exp.c: Incorrect. This is a hard limit that cannot be increased.
exp.d: Incorrect. Root account keys should never be used.
